newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak bourse continues to decline, SAX down.
newsitem.headline: Slovak bourse continues to decline, SAX down.

text.p: 1620 GMT - Slovak blue chips ease in listless trading on the Bratislava Stock Exchange on Monday, with the SAX index closing 2.42 points at 165.52 points.
*Slovnaft did not trade, VSZ down 20 at 480, VUB bank up nine at 1,680 crowns, Nafta did not trade
Slovak blue chips eased in listless trading on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Monday, as the SAX index closed down 2.42 points at 165.52.
Brokers said that foreign investors appeared to be showing limited signs of revived interest in trading after the bourse's three-month decline resulted in significantly lower share prices.
"Some prices are getting attractive, but it is a question of who will sell their shares so cheaply," Dusan Sykora of ING Barings said.
Most blue chips did not trade at all on Monday, and only 188 shares were traded on the automated listed market.

Steel maker VSZ was one of the few that did see some activity, losing 20 crowns to close at 480 while commercial bank VUB closed up nine crowns at 1,680 crowns, but lost 0.18 percent in the average price.
"It seems that those who were keeping the VUB price artificially high during the past months, have lost their patience," Sykora said. "I expect a further decline in VUB in the near future," he added.
